research_text:
## Research brief

### API and finding

`java.security.spec.X509EncodedKeySpec` represents an encoded **public key**, specifically the ASN.1 `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` structure. Oracle’s JCA guide describes the representation as DER-encoded. It is not a representation of an entire X.509 certificate or a private key. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/spec/X509EncodedKeySpec.html))

For the supplied rule, the reported missing preparation refers to the `encodedKey` byte array passed to the rule’s constructor event. The rule requires the analysis predicate `preparedKeyMaterial[encodedKey]`; it does **not** define that predicate or a runtime test for it. A report therefore indicates that the required predicate was not established by the analysis, not that the material was necessarily unprepared at runtime. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/X509EncodedKeySpec.crysl))

### Documented usage and remediation

Oracle documents the following API contract:

- Supply a non-null byte array assumed to contain the X.509-encoded public key. The constructor copies the array; `getEncoded()` returns a new array on each call. The constructor documentation states the encoding assumption but does not promise to validate it. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/spec/X509EncodedKeySpec.html))
- To obtain a `PublicKey`, Oracle shows passing the specification to an algorithm-appropriate `KeyFactory.generatePublic`. That method documents `InvalidKeySpecException` when the specification is inappropriate for the factory. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyFactory.html))
- `Key.getEncoded()` can return `null` if a key does not support encoding. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/Key.html))

The sources establish the expected format and show conversion through `KeyFactory`; they do **not** prescribe a specific remediation for a `preparedKeyMaterial` finding or define which preparation steps satisfy that predicate. Nor do they establish that a successful conversion authenticates the key’s provenance or trust.

### Compatibility and migration

- **Persisted and wire formats:** Oracle describes the key encoding as usable outside the JVM, including for transmission and storage. Existing consumers expecting this representation depend on the relevant X.509 `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` encoding. The sources do not specify a format migration for this finding. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))
- **Platform versions:** The class is documented since Java 1.2. The two-argument constructor accepting an algorithm name is documented since Java 9; Java 8 documents only the one-argument constructor. These statements concern Java SE; they do not establish Android or individual provider compatibility. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/spec/X509EncodedKeySpec.html))
- **Documented conversion:** `KeyFactory` can convert between compatible key specifications and key objects; Oracle gives DSA encoded and component-based specifications as an example. This is a conversion facility, not a prescribed migration for the finding. Compatibility of any particular persisted data, peer, algorithm, and provider remains to be determined. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyFactory.html))

### Exact rule

The published rule’s matching and predicate clauses are: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/X509EncodedKeySpec.crysl))

```crysl
SPEC java.security.spec.X509EncodedKeySpec

OBJECTS
	byte[] encodedKey;

EVENTS
	c1: X509EncodedKeySpec(encodedKey);
	Con := c1;

ORDER
	Con

REQUIRES
	preparedKeyMaterial[encodedKey];

ENSURES
	speccedKey[this, _] after Con;
```

The declared event is the **one-argument constructor** of the specified `java.security.spec.X509EncodedKeySpec` type, with `encodedKey` declared as `byte[]`; it does not declare an ordinary receiver-method event or the two-argument constructor. It requires `preparedKeyMaterial[encodedKey]` and declares `speccedKey[this, _]` after `Con`.

**No:** the rule does not declare a match for an unrelated method or type merely because it shares the name `X509EncodedKeySpec`. Whether a particular detector implementation resolves a call incorrectly cannot be determined from this rule file alone. The file also gives no algorithm, key-size, trust-anchor, certificate-chain, or subsequent-use constraints. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/X509EncodedKeySpec.crysl))

### Source limits

The rule URL points to the mutable `master` branch. The retrieved text was inspected, but its SHA-256 was **not independently verified** against the supplied hash. No local finding, call target, predicate producer, deployed behavior, or migration environment was inspected.

- Rule: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/X509EncodedKeySpec.crysl
- Oracle API: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/spec/X509EncodedKeySpec.html
- Oracle `KeyFactory` API: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyFactory.html
- Oracle JCA guide: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html
